questions.q: What is a "base table" like task or cmdb_ci?
options: A table that only administrators can ever query
A deliberately generic, foundational table meant to be extended by more specific tables
A temporary table deleted after each upgrade
A table used exclusively for reporting dashboards
questions.explain: Base tables hold the fields and behavior many specific record types share, without committing to any one of them.

questions.q: What does it mean that incident "extends" task?
options: Incident copies task's fields once and the two tables are never related again
Incident replaces task entirely once the Incident application is installed
Extension means incident records are stored only in memory, never on disk
Incident inherits every field task has and adds its own fields (like caller_id and category) on top
questions.explain: Table extension is ServiceNow's inheritance mechanism — the child table gets all of the parent's fields plus whatever it adds itself.

questions.q: Which sys_db_object field records that incident extends task?
options: Assignment group
Short description
Extends table
sys_mod_count
questions.explain: The "Extends table" field on a table's sys_db_object record points to its parent table, if any.

questions.q: What happens when you query the task table directly with no further filter?
options: Incidents, problems, change requests, and other task-extending records are all returned together, since each one is technically a task
The query fails because task has no records of its own
Only problem records are returned
Only custom tables that extend task are returned
questions.explain: Because incident, problem, and change_request all extend task, every one of their records also satisfies a query against task.

questions.q: Why do Incident, Problem, and Change Management behave so consistently with each other in ServiceNow (same state field, same priority calculation)?
options: They don't actually share any technical structure, only similar names
ServiceNow synchronizes their fields nightly through a scheduled job
They are all stored in sys_dictionary instead of being real tables
All three extend the same base table, task, so shared logic is defined once and inherited everywhere
questions.explain: Because they all extend task, fields like state, assignment_group, and priority logic are defined once on the base table and inherited by all three.
